items.material:
THE PHOTOGRAPH WITH A NEW CAPTION
A dramatic photograph appeared in our class chat with the caption, 'Our river flooded this morning.' Before forwarding it, Jia asked where the picture came from. The first message she saw had no link, location or date. She found an earlier public post showing the same bridge and the same broken fence, but it described a different town several years earlier. That comparison was enough to challenge the new caption; it was not enough to explain every detail of the original event.
Jia told the group what she had checked and what remained unknown. She did not accuse every person who had shared it of deliberately lying. She also checked the current notice from the relevant local authority before making any claim about conditions near her own school. A striking image can be genuine while the words attached to it are misleading. Checking the origin and the current local situation are related tasks, but they answer different questions.

Reader's illustration note:
Both cards repeat exactly the same original fictional illustration, not an actual news photograph. The illustration shows a bridge and a broken fence; it supplies no real location or date. The labels restate the two contexts described in the report.
Card A says: Another town · several years earlier.
Card B says: Our river · this morning.

transfer.passage:
A FICTIONAL GATE-PHOTO CHECK
A class message uses a picture of a fallen tree to claim, 'Our school gate is blocked today.' An earlier public post shows the same bench and cracked wall in a different park last year. That match challenges the new caption; it does not explain every detail of the earlier event. A current local notice separately says that one path by the sports ground is closed today and the school-gate route is open. These are the places and conditions covered by that notice. The class has not checked every sharer’s intention.

options.text: Question the picture’s new local caption, and use the current notice for the named path and gate route.
Question the picture’s new local caption, so conclude that no route anywhere can be closed today.
Use the current notice about the closed path, and conclude that every sharer deliberately lied.

answer.display: Question the picture’s new local caption, and use the current notice for the named path and gate route.
